A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the luminosity of an e+e- heteroenergetic system is likely to reach the same value as that of a homoenergetic system.
the luminosity of the system is likely to fall below 10^33 cm^-2 sec^-1, unless the tune shift can be kept below 10^-4.
, for heteroenergetic systems, the luminosity is likely to be limited by the tune-shift effect, but that the tune-shift effect can be reduced by increasing the beam energy ratio.
The main takeaway from our work is that
heteroenergetic systems are likely to have a luminosity advantage over homogeneously energized systems only when the energy spread of one or both beams is small.
the tune-shift limit is likely to be more severe in heteroenergetic systems than in systems with equal-energy beams.
